newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to complete SFP sale by mid-1997 -minister.
newsitem.headline: France to complete SFP sale by mid-1997 -minister.

text.p: The French government expects to complete its privatisation of the SFP film studio by mid-1997, Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy said on Thursday.
He told Les Echos daily in an interview that an offer by Generale des Eaux and Havas was the best from an industrial point of view and involved no redundancies.
The government said on Tuesday it wanted to sell loss-making Societe Francaise de Production to a consortium of Generale and Havas, conditional on approval by the privatisation commission.
It said it would inject up to 1.2 billion francs into SFP, of which 350 million would be paid before the end of 1996.

"Looking at the time necessary for the European Commission, the privatisation commisssion and the employees' council to give their opinions, it seems very reasonable to expect completion before the middle of 1997," Douste-Blazy told Les Echos.
Douste-Blazy said the full cost of SFP to French taxpayers since 1990 will have been 3.4 billion francs once the capital injection associated with the sale is carried out.
That included a basic sum of 3.1 billion francs paid by governments and the rest was interest, he said.

The government said on Tuesday that the new cash injection was needed because of the company's financial and economic situation. It would allow future shareholders to run normal operating risks and would also contribute 40 percent of the cost of a job reduction plan.
Douste-Blazy told Les Echos there would be no forced lay-offs as a result of the sale.

There had been four offers for SFP on the table. One was by Global Studios run by French businessman Walter Butler, another by Little Big One (LBO) run by Swiss investor Frabrice Giger and a third by former SFP director Jean Cressant.
The fourth was made by Havas' Images Television International and Generale des Eaux's Generale des Images.
All the bids demanded a capital injection from the government in exchange for maintaining jobs.
